intro.data: Just as every kind of data has a do-nothing step that hands it back untouched (the identity, back in Chapter 1), there's a do-nothing converter that turns a List into the very same List, unchanged. Here both wrappers are List. One choice keeps each list exactly as it is; the other pads in a default and changes it. Pick the keep-as-is converter for every kind of data.
intro.alchemy: Just as every reagent has a do-nothing step that hands it back untouched, there's a do-nothing method that turns a rack of vials into the very same rack, unchanged. Here both sides are racks. One choice keeps each rack exactly as it is; the other adds a blank vial and changes it. Pick the keep-as-is method for every reagent.
intro.spellcraft: Just as every essence has a do-nothing step that hands it back untouched, there's a do-nothing working that turns a stack of runes into the very same stack, unchanged. Here both sides are stacks. One choice keeps each stack exactly as it is; the other adds a blank rune and changes it. Choose the keep-as-is working for every essence.
intro.abstract: When F = G, the identity transformation id_F : F ⇒ F has the identity component id at every object. One distractor is typed right but not natural. Build id_F.

afterSuccess.data: Keeping each list untouched is the do-nothing rule — it changes nothing, so it always agrees with itself. padDefault looked right but altered the list, so it failed. This do-nothing rule is the identity: the natural transformation that leaves a wrapper exactly as it is.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Keeping each rack untouched is the do-nothing rule — it changes nothing, so it always agrees with itself. 'Add a Vial' looked right but altered the rack, so it failed. This do-nothing rule is the identity: it leaves a container exactly as it is.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Keeping each stack untouched is the do-nothing rule — it changes nothing, so it always agrees with itself. 'Add a Rune' looked right but altered the stack, so it failed. This do-nothing rule is the identity: it leaves a container exactly as it is.
afterSuccess.abstract: Identity components everywhere give id_F : F ⇒ F, the identity of the functor category [C, D]. The padding family is typed right but not natural.

reveal.summary: For any functor F there is an identity natural transformation id_F : F ⇒ F (the identity component at each object). It is the identity morphism in the functor category [C, D].
reveal.moreFormal: Functor categories [C, D] have functors as objects and natural transformations as morphisms, composed component-wise. id_F is each object's identity — the unit of that composition (a future chapter).
reveal.programmerAnalogy: The identity polymorphic function id<A>: F<A> => F<A> — changes nothing, natural everywhere.
